runs.failure_point: It opened the second matter of one client but named only the sibling, and the answer adds matters without the clause.

first_error.why: It read a diligence memo of the second matter of the same client at [57]-[62] but the answer names only the sibling matter for that client.
first_error.critic_note: No review named the matter; it had been opened, so it never appeared in the unopened lists

other_errors.why: The answer lists the sibling matter, a settlement-agreement matter, another transaction matter and several M&A diligence matters as containing the clause.
other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) the review at [80] flagged possible over-inclusion; the next stage raised the counts instead

divergence: All three runs failed the same way in outcome: each found the hit set with store-wide extraction scans and listed a sibling matter of one client in place of the second matter of that client, and each over-included. They split at where that matter was lost: T0 never opened it (surfaced-not-opened at the first screening stage), T1 listed its files and excluded it, plus a second needed matter, at the write stage, and T2 read a memo from it but named only the sibling at the write stage (both under-inclusion). Only in T0 did the reviews name the matter, in their list of surfaced matters never opened; the agent opened other matters but not this one.
